## Cross-Source Dependencies
- CIPHER sampling consumes BASTION flow paths and GARNET hypotheses [CIPHER, BASTION, GARNET].
- DELTA pump sequencing depends on BASTION pressure and ECHO power [DELTA, BASTION, ECHO].
- FALCON treatment selection depends on GARNET source hypotheses [FALCON, GARNET].
- INDIGO telemetry supports BASTION, DELTA, ECHO, FALCON but each retains own decision gate [INDIGO, BASTION, DELTA, ECHO, FALCON].
- HELIX audit events consumed by INDIGO; HELIX does not authorize access [HELIX, INDIGO].
- JASPER environmental notices depend on GARNET source impact and FALCON discharge conditions [JASPER, GARNET, FALCON].
- KESTREL fuel supports ECHO generator duration; KESTREL chemicals support FALCON staging [KESTREL, ECHO, FALCON].
- LUMEN communications depend on CIPHER/AURORA advisory status and INDIGO/BASTION service observations [LUMEN, CIPHER, AURORA, INDIGO, BASTION].
- MOSAIC candidate changes make BASTION, CIPHER, DELTA, ECHO, FALCON, HELIX evidence stale [MOSAIC, BASTION, CIPHER, DELTA, ECHO, FALCON, HELIX].
- NEXUS consumes all sources for independent review but does not mutate states [NEXUS, ALL].

## Conflicts and Unknowns
- GARNET ash-plume 34% is forecast, not observed contamination; reservoir (non-detect) vs river intake (3.1 µg/L) must not be merged [GARNET].
- Chemical yard investigation hold active; trench inspection below grade pending [GARNET].
- INDIGO 4% unobserved coverage does not prove healthy uninstrumented zones [INDIGO].
- HELIX break-glass access expired; remote automation restoration requires named evidence [HELIX].
- NEXUS blocking findings: second-round samples incomplete, generator transfer evidence stale, PH duty officer acknowledgment missing [NEXUS].

## Candidate Currency
Current candidate W7 (H12, P9, T6, W4) [MOSAIC]. Any mutation to hydraulic model, pump plan, treatment plan, key set, valve map, or firmware makes prior evidence stale and requires recheck [MOSAIC]. Rollback to W6 mechanically possible only with V8/C11 compatibility but not authorized [MOSAIC].

## Falsifiers for Important Claims
- If CIPHER second-round samples show benzene ≥5.0 µg/L at any location, clearance claim falsified [CIPHER].
- If ECHO generator transfer evidence remains stale after recheck, 36-hr duration claim falsified [ECHO].
- If AURORA public-health duty officer does not acknowledge, closure claim falsified [AURORA].
- If FALCON turbidity exceeds 0.30 NTU for >4 hrs, release gate claim falsified [FALCON].
- If INDIGO coverage drops below 96% or unobserved zones show adverse conditions, telemetry adequacy claim falsified [INDIGO].

# Solace Water Recovery Decision

## Authority, scope, and restoration decision
The Solace County Water Recovery Decision is governed by the authority that only the county health officer may lift a do-not-drink order, and only after current laboratory and distribution-system verification; a utility repair or green mechanical check is not public-health authorization [AURORA]. Final closure requires the utility director to accept every declared blocker and residual risk [AURORA]. BASTION and CIPHER supply hydraulic and laboratory evidence but cannot lift health restrictions [AURORA]. The current recovery candidate is W7 with hydraulic model H12, pump plan P9, treatment plan T6, and key set W4; evidence for W6 is historical unless explicitly transferred and rechecked [MOSAIC]. Rollback to W6 is mechanically possible only while valve map V8 and controller firmware C11 remain compatible, but mechanical possibility is not authorization [MOSAIC]. Every mutation must record before and after candidate hashes, changed files, affected evidence, check currency, owner, and rollback effect [MOSAIC].

## Hydraulics, storage, and zone sequencing
The north-zone distribution system currently holds a minimum pressure of 42 psi [BASTION]. Ridge storage contains 5.8 million gallons, while the twelve-hour emergency reserve is 3.2 million gallons; these are distinct measures and must not be conflated as treated reserve [BASTION]. DELTA pump sequencing depends on BASTION pressure and ECHO power; cavitation constraints limit shared-main capacity under staged demand conditions [DELTA, BASTION, ECHO]. Pressure warnings at 38 psi and isolation triggers at 30 psi are distinct control states: a warning does not initiate isolation, and an isolation trigger does not merely warn [INDIGO, BASTION]. Residence time in the distribution loop must be verified against candidate-bound hydraulic model H12; any change to valve map V8 or controller firmware C11 invalidates prior residence-time evidence [MOSAIC]. The current minimum pressure of 42 psi exceeds the 30 psi isolation trigger but remains within the operational band defined by H12; no isolation action is currently indicated [BASTION, INDIGO].

## Sampling, source water, and treatment barriers
Clearance requires two complete sampling rounds spaced at least sixteen hours apart; one clean round is insufficient [CIPHER]. The benzene reporting limit is 0.5 micrograms per liter and the action threshold is 5.0 micrograms per liter; these are distinct controls and must not be conflated, as a reporting limit indicates analytical capability while an action threshold triggers public-health response [CIPHER]. CIPHER sample placement consumes BASTION flow paths and GARNET contamination hypotheses; any change to hydraulic routing or source-water characterization makes prior sampling evidence stale [CIPHER, BASTION, GARNET]. Current volatile-organic screening is non-detect at the reservoir and 3.1 micrograms per liter at the river intake; these locations must not be merged, as they represent distinct hydrological positions with different contamination probabilities [GARNET]. The ash-plume model assigns a 34 percent chance of intake impact during the next rain event, which is a forecast probability, not measured contamination [GARNET]. The investigation hold remains active for the chemical yard because the containment trench has not been inspected below grade; this hold blocks clearance until resolved [GARNET]. Staleness applies: any candidate-bound hydraulic, pump, treatment, or source-water change invalidates prior sampling rounds and requires re-sampling per CIPHER protocol [CIPHER, MOSAIC].

## Power, pumping, logistics, and demand stages
Emergency generation can carry 4.1 MW for thirty-six hours at the current fuel stock; the duration is not thirty-six days and excludes mobile-pump load [ECHO]. The grid feed is rated at 8.2 MW, but the damaged switchgear limits current delivery to 6.5 MW; rated power is not usable power [ECHO]. KESTREL diesel stock covers emergency load for 36 hours and full pump load for 22 hours; these load regimes are distinct and must not be merged as a single duration [KESTREL, ECHO]. Coagulant and chlorine chemical stocks provide 4.5 days and 3.2 days of treatment capacity respectively; inventory duration is not delivery lead time [KESTREL, FALCON]. Staffing continuity depends on mutual-aid logistics; current shift coverage must be verified against the 36-hour generator window [KESTREL]. Any change to ECHO power state or KESTREL fuel stock makes prior pump sequencing evidence stale [DELTA, ECHO, KESTREL]. The shared-main limit under staged demand requires that DELTA pump capacity not exceed the 6.5 MW usable grid feed plus any available generator margin without triggering cavitation constraints [DELTA, ECHO, BASTION].

## Treatment barriers, turbidity, disinfectant, and source blend
Free chlorine must remain between 0.8 and 2.0 milligrams per liter at entry points and at least 0.2 mg/L in distribution; these are distinct controls with different thresholds and units of measure [FALCON]. Current combined-filter turbidity is 0.18 NTU, with a release gate at or below 0.30 NTU sustained for four hours; the 0.18 NTU value is a turbidity measurement, not a chlorine residual [FALCON]. Source blending must account for GARNET contamination hypotheses: the river intake shows 3.1 µg/L volatile-organics while the reservoir remains non-detect, requiring distinct treatment paths and contact times [GARNET, FALCON]. Treatment plan T6 governs current disinfectant dosing and turbidity controls; any change to source blend or turbidity profile invalidates prior treatment evidence [MOSAIC, FALCON, GARNET]. The emergency dechlorination residual limit at outfall is ≤0.019 mg/L under permit E-17; exceeding this requires immediate stop of discharge [JASPER, FALCON]. Contact time verification must be rechecked after any hydraulic model change to H12 or valve map modification to V8 [MOSAIC, FALCON, BASTION].

## Contamination hypotheses, investigation holds, and falsifiers
The ash-plume model assigns a 34 percent chance of intake impact during the next rain event; this is a forecast probability, not observed contamination, and must be distinguished from measured values [GARNET]. Volatile-organic screening shows non-detect at the reservoir and 3.1 µg/L at the river intake; these locations are hydrologically distinct and must not be merged into a single source-water characterization [GARNET]. The chemical yard investigation hold remains active because the containment trench has not been inspected below grade; this hold blocks any claim of complete source-water clearance [GARNET]. Falsifiers for important claims include: if CIPHER second-round samples show benzene ≥5.0 µg/L at any location, the clearance claim is falsified [CIPHER]; if GARNET river-intake measurements exceed 5.0 µg/L after the next rain event, the 34% forecast underestimates actual contamination [GARNET, CIPHER]; if FALCON turbidity exceeds 0.30 NTU for more than four hours, the release gate claim is falsified [FALCON]. Any new observation at the river intake that contradicts the non-detect reservoir value requires re-evaluation of source blending under T6 [GARNET, FALCON, MOSAIC].

## Access, control-system integrity, and evidence custody
The exposed SCADA service token was revoked at 14:10 UTC [HELIX]. The controller signing key was not exposed and remains current under key-set version W4; break-glass access expires after two hours and requires dual approval plus immutable session logging, meaning emergency access is not continuing authorization [HELIX]. Online control logs are retained for ninety days and archived incident evidence for seven years; these periods serve different obligations and must not be conflated as a single retention policy [HELIX]. Automation restoration requires named evidence of key integrity, token rotation, and controller firmware state; a green mechanical check does not establish control-system readiness [HELIX, MOSAIC]. Immutable custody of audit events is consumed by INDIGO telemetry but HELIX does not authorize access independently [HELIX, INDIGO]. Any change to key-set W4, valve map V8, or controller firmware C11 invalidates prior access and automation evidence and requires re-verification under MOSAIC lineage rules [MOSAIC, HELIX]. Rollback of control-system state is possible only while V8 and C11 compatibility persists; mechanical rollback does not constitute operational authorization [MOSAIC, HELIX].

## Telemetry coverage, alerts, delays, and uncertainty
Critical-signal telemetry coverage stands at 96 percent, with 4 percent of monitored points unobserved; this coverage gap does not prove the uninstrumented zones are healthy, only that they are not currently observable [INDIGO]. Pressure warnings at 38 psi and isolation triggers at 30 psi are distinct control states; a warning does not initiate isolation, and an isolation trigger does not merely warn [INDIGO, BASTION]. Telemetry delays in the unobserved 4 percent create uncertainty that must be treated as potential adverse condition until verified by direct observation or alternate telemetry [INDIGO]. Warnings versus actions: a pressure warning at 38 psi requires monitoring and logging but does not require isolation; an isolation trigger at 30 psi requires immediate valve closure and zone separation [INDIGO, BASTION]. Any change to hydraulic model H12, pump plan P9, or control-system key set W4 invalidates prior telemetry correlation evidence and requires re-verification of coverage and alert thresholds [MOSAIC, INDIGO, BASTION, DELTA, ECHO, FALCON]. Alternate telemetry paths must be identified for the 4 percent unobserved zone before closure can be claimed [INDIGO, NEXUS].

## Environmental determination, notice clock, permits, and discharge
The unauthorized discharge notice clock is 72 hours from the determination event, not from detection time; AURORA owns materiality of the determination [JASPER]. The emergency dechlorination residual limit at outfall is ≤0.019 mg/L under permit E-17; exceeding this requires immediate stop of discharge and triggers the notice clock [JASPER, FALCON]. Environmental notices depend on GARNET source impact and FALCON discharge conditions; a change in either invalidates prior environmental evidence [JASPER, GARNET, FALCON]. Evidence custody for environmental records follows HELIX retention: 90 days online, 7 years archived incident evidence [HELIX, JASPER]. The determination event that starts the 72-hour clock must be documented with timestamp, responsible officer, and supporting laboratory or telemetry evidence; a forecast probability from GARNET does not constitute a determination event [JASPER, GARNET, AURORA]. Any discharge exceeding permit limits requires immediate public notification under LUMEN protocols in addition to environmental agency notice [JASPER, LUMEN, FALCON].

## Public advisories, accessibility, alternate water, and communications
Do-not-drink notice delivery coverage reaches 91 percent of registered endpoints; the missing 9 percent represents communication uncertainty, not a reduction in affected population [LUMEN]. Call center capacity is 3,200 calls per hour for six hours, while forecast demand is 4,100 calls per hour; alternate-language outreach may reduce repeat calls but does not eliminate the gap [LUMEN]. Public advisories depend on CIPHER/AURORA advisory status and INDIGO/BASTION service observations; any change in clearance status or hydraulic state requires immediate re-issuance [LUMEN, CIPHER, AURORA, INDIGO, BASTION]. Accessibility requirements mandate that alternate water sources be identified for the 9 percent unregistered population; this is a service obligation, not a telemetry gap [LUMEN, KESTREL]. Service states must be communicated distinctly: do-not-drink, boil-water, and normal-service are separate public-health states with different required actions [LUMEN, AURORA, CIPHER]. Any change to advisory status requires re-verification of delivery coverage and accessibility compliance before the next communication cycle [LUMEN, MOSAIC].

## Candidate lineage, rollback, effect uptake, checks, blockers, and closure
Current candidate W7 (H12, P9, T6, W4) is the operative recovery state; W6 evidence is historical unless explicitly transferred and rechecked under MOSAIC rules [MOSAIC]. Rollback to W6 is mechanically possible only while valve map V8 and controller firmware C11 remain compatible; mechanical possibility is not authorization [MOSAIC]. Effect uptake: any mutation to hydraulic model, pump plan, treatment plan, key set, valve map, or firmware makes prior evidence stale and requires recheck before any operational decision can be made on the basis of that evidence [MOSAIC, BASTION, CIPHER, DELTA, ECHO, FALCON, HELIX]. Current checks bind to the exact candidate; any later effect makes the prior check stale and invalidates readiness claims based on that check [MOSAIC, NEXUS]. Blocking findings include: incomplete second-round samples under CIPHER protocol, stale generator transfer evidence under ECHO, and missing public-health duty officer acknowledgment under AURORA [NEXUS, CIPHER, ECHO, AURORA]. Independent readiness review by NEXUS consumes all sources but does not mutate states; no self-authorization of readiness is permitted [NEXUS, AURORA]. Closure requires the utility director to accept every declared blocker and residual risk after independent review confirms that all blocking findings are resolved [AURORA, NEXUS]. Submission of this decision does not establish readiness; it proposes submission for independent review only when the package is genuinely ready [AURORA, NEXUS, MOSAIC].
